context: The 10 solid nodes are connected as follows. Root 1 has left child 2 and right child 3. Node 2 has only a left child, 4. Node 3 has left child 6 and right child 7. Node 4 has left child 8 and right child 9. Node 6 has only a left child, 12, and node 7 has only a right child, 15. Nodes 8, 9, 12, and 15 are leaves. The array has 15 slots at indices 0 through 14. It holds 10 node values, with empty slots at indices 4, 9, 10, 12, and 13. The table lists the contents of each slot.

frames.explanation: Although there is no node at index 4, its two child positions on the next level, 9 and 10, must also stay empty so that later nodes do not shift forward. For example, node 6 at index 5 has value 12 at its left child position, 11, and an empty slot at its right child position, 12.
frames.title: Binary tree array with empty slots preserved

result: Keeping internal empty slots makes it possible to reconstruct this tree uniquely using the child positions 2i+1 and 2i+2 for index i. An empty slot indicates that there is no node there (often written as None or null in code). It does not represent the value 0.
summary: Explicitly keeping slots for missing nodes within a level-order array lets the mappings 2i+1 and 2i+2 reconstruct the tree shape uniquely.
title: Binary tree array with empty slots preserved
